NAVY 101.description: The Naval Service with emphasis on the mission, organization, regulation, and components of the Navy and Marine Corps.
NAVY 101.subject: NAVY
NAVY 101.title: Fundamentals of Naval Science

NAVY 102.description: A historical survey on the importance of military doctrine and the many roles of the United States Military covering from the American Revolution to present day. HIST 468 or ARMY 406 may be taken in lieu of this course to meet the Naval ROTC History requirement.
NAVY 102.subject: NAVY
NAVY 102.title: U.S. Military History

NAVY 111.description: Military drill, cruise preparation, customs, traditions, and special areas of knowledge required of commissioned officers in the Navy and Marine Corps. Pass/Fail grading.
NAVY 111.subject: NAVY
NAVY 111.title: Naval Military Laboratory

NAVY 201.description: Types, structure, and purpose of naval ships. Hydrodynamic forces, stability, compartmentation, electrical, and auxiliary systems. Theory of design and operation of steam, gas turbine, and nuclear propulsion. Shipboard safety and firefighting.
NAVY 201.subject: NAVY
NAVY 201.title: Naval Ships Systems I

NAVY 202.description: Fire control systems, weapons types, capabilities, and limitations. Physical aspects of radar and underwater sound for target acquisition, threat analysis, tracking, weapons selection, delivery, and guidance. Explosives, fusing, and naval ordnance.
NAVY 202.subject: NAVY
NAVY 202.title: Naval Ships Systems II

NAVY 301.description: Piloting and celestial navigation theory, principles, and procedures. Tides, current, weather, use of navigational instruments and equipments, and practicum. Laboratory required.
NAVY 301.subject: NAVY
NAVY 301.title: Navigation/Naval Operations I

NAVY 301L.description: Laboratory work in piloting and celestial navigation to complement Naval Science 301. One hour per week.
NAVY 301L.subject: NAVY
NAVY 301L.title: Navigation/Naval Operations Lab I

NAVY 302.description: International and Inland Rules of the Road; relative motion-vector analysis; ship handling, employment, tactics, and afloat communications; and operations analysis. Laboratory required.
NAVY 302.subject: NAVY
NAVY 302.title: Navigation/Naval Operations II

NAVY 302L.description: Laboratory work in maneuvering board (vector analysis) and Rules of the Road to complement Naval Science 302. One hour per week.
NAVY 302L.subject: NAVY
NAVY 302L.title: Navigation/Naval Operations II Lab

NAVY 303.description: A survey of military history emphasizing principles of warfare, strategy and tactics, and significant military leaders and organizations.
NAVY 303.subject: NAVY
NAVY 303.title: Evolution of the Art of War

NAVY 401.description: Theory and principles of management, focusing on the officer-manager as an organizational decision maker. Includes interpersonal skills; behavior factors; group dynamics.
NAVY 401.subject: NAVY
NAVY 401.title: Naval Leadership and Management I

NAVY 402.description: Integration of professional military competencies and qualities of effective leadership with emphasis on moral and ethical responsibilities, accountability, communications, and military law for the junior officer.
NAVY 402.subject: NAVY
NAVY 402.title: Naval Leadership and Ethics

NAVY 403.description: The history of Maneuver Warfare emphasizing doctrine and techniques while enabling students to become critical thinkers and better prepare them for future service.
NAVY 403.subject: NAVY
NAVY 403.title: Fundamentals of Maneuver Warfare
